title: EXDATE removes an instance the RRULE generates

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.8.5.3 (Recurrence Rule)
normative.quote: the 'EXDATE' property ... take precedence over those specified by inclusion properties (i.e., RDATE and RRULE)

expect.note: COUNT=5 generates five candidates; EXDATE removes one, so four remain. COUNT bounds generation, not the final set.

rationale: The COUNT-versus-EXDATE interaction is the corpus's cheapest test of whether an engine composes the set correctly or applies EXDATE before COUNT.

title: RDATE adds an instance outside the RRULE

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.8.5.2 (Recurrence Date-Times)
normative.quote: This property can be specified in recurring 'VEVENT' ... to define a set of instances

expect.note: The RDATE instance is merged in date order, not appended.

rationale: Ordering of merged RDATEs is a common bug and is directly observable.

title: EXDATE takes precedence over RDATE for the same instant

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.8.5.3 (Recurrence Rule)
normative.quote: the 'EXDATE' property ... take precedence over those specified by inclusion properties (i.e., RDATE and RRULE)

expect.note: The explicitly added instance is explicitly removed; EXDATE wins.

rationale: The precedence rule is normative and unambiguous, which makes it a useful control against the genuinely ambiguous precedence vector SET-004.

title: EXDATE with VALUE=DATE against a DATE-TIME DTSTART (erratum 6316, open since 2020)

normative.title: RFC 5545 erratum 6316 (REPORTED since 2020-10-22, §3.8.5.1 EXDATE value type)
normative.note: REPORTED 2020-10-22, still not Verified six years on: asks whether a DATE-only EXDATE excludes all instances occurring on that date

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.8.5.1 (Exception Date-Times)
normative.note: the property definition permits VALUE=DATE but does not say how it matches DATE-TIME instances

cases.label: exclude-whole-day
cases.note: The reading erratum 6316 proposes: a DATE-valued EXDATE removes every instance on that date.

cases.label: exclude-midnight-only
cases.note: The literal reading: DATE 20260106 is 20260106T000000, which no instance equals, so nothing is excluded.

cases.label: reject
cases.note: Engines requiring EXDATE's value type to equal DTSTART's — the position erratum 6316 asks the RFC to take.

expect.note: Six years as a Reported erratum with no resolution.

python-dateutil@tz2026a.error: TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes

python-dateutil@tz2026c.error: TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes

rationale: A live, unresolved specification question in the most safety-relevant direction: an EXDATE that fails to exclude is a job that runs when someone said it must not. Three shipped behaviours, no arbiter.

title: EXDATE naming an instant the rule never generates

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.8.5.1 (Exception Date-Times)
normative.note: no statement about an EXDATE that matches nothing

cases.label: silent
cases.note: The overwhelmingly common behaviour.

cases.label: warn
cases.note: Same set, plus a diagnostic. Distinguishable only via the runner's diagnostics channel.

cases.label: reject
cases.note: Treat a no-op EXDATE as an authoring error.

rationale: A typo in an EXDATE — the wrong minute, the wrong zone — is silently a no-op in every mainstream engine, and the consequence is a job that runs on a day someone explicitly excluded. Worth a policy axis in any new product.

title: EXDATE in a different zone naming the same instant

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.8.5.1 (Exception Date-Times)
normative.note: no statement about whether EXDATE matching is by instant or by (zone, wall time) pair

cases.label: instant-match
cases.note: 2026-01-06T14:00 London is 2026-01-06T09:00 New York — the same instant, so the instance is removed.

cases.label: wall-time-match
cases.note: Engines comparing (zone, wall time) pairs find no match and remove nothing.

rationale: Occurrence identity in one vector. If instances are instants, the first answer is right; if they are zone-qualified wall times, the second is. RFC 5545 never says, and the choice propagates into every deduplication and cancellation feature built on top.

title: Duplicate instants from RRULE and RDATE are coalesced

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.8.5.3 (Recurrence Rule)
normative.quote: Where duplicate instances are generated by the 'RRULE' and 'RDATE' properties, only one recurrence is considered.

rationale: An explicit normative de-duplication requirement that is trivially testable and not universally implemented.

title: Two RRULEs in one component

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.8.5.3 (Recurrence Rule)
normative.note: the property may appear more than once per the component grammar, but the specification deprecates it without forbidding it and does not define the combination

cases.label: union
cases.note: Set union, each rule bounded by its own COUNT.

cases.label: first-only
cases.note: Engines that keep only the first RRULE — the most common behaviour, and a silent data loss.

rationale: Multiple RRULEs are legal syntax, deprecated prose, and undefined semantics. Silently dropping the second rule is the modal behaviour and is invisible to the author.

title: Every instance excluded: an empty recurrence set

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.8.5.3 (Recurrence Rule)
normative.note: no statement about a fully excluded set

cases.label: empty
cases.note: Return an empty set — the reading consistent with EXDATE precedence.

cases.label: reject
cases.note: Treat a component with no instances as invalid.

rationale: Empty is a legitimate answer that many APIs cannot express (an iterator that raises StopIteration on the first call is indistinguishable from an error to some callers). Paired with CRON-INV-007 and RRULE-CORE-018.

title: EXRULE (removed from RFC 5545, present in RFC 2445)

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.8.5.3 (Recurrence Rule)
normative.note: RFC 5545 removed EXRULE, which RFC 2445 defined; the property is therefore legal iCalendar under one standard and unknown under its successor

cases.label: rfc2445
cases.note: Engines retaining RFC 2445 support (dateutil's rruleset has exrule) exclude the weekend days.

cases.label: ignore
cases.note: Engines that ignore unknown properties emit the full daily set — including the weekend the author excluded.

rationale: A property whose removal from a standard silently changes the meaning of existing data. The 'ignore' outcome runs jobs on days that were explicitly excluded, which is the same failure class as SET-004.

title: RDATE with a PERIOD value

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.8.5.2 (Recurrence Date-Times)
normative.quote: Value Type: The default value type for this property is DATE-TIME. The value type can be set to DATE or PERIOD.

cases.label: supported
cases.note: The period's start becomes the instance; its duration overrides the component's.

cases.label: reject
cases.note: Most recurrence-only libraries have no duration concept and cannot represent this at all.

rrule-go@tz2026a.error: strToDates failed: bad dates param: unsupported: VALUE=PERIOD

rationale: PERIOD-valued RDATE is the only place RFC 5545 lets a single occurrence carry a different *magnitude* from its siblings — the construct Stripe's prorated stub period needs and that no pure recurrence library models.

title: RDATE before DTSTART

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.8.5.2 (Recurrence Date-Times)
normative.note: no statement that RDATE values must be at or after DTSTART

cases.label: include
cases.note: The recurrence set now starts before its own DTSTART.

cases.label: drop
cases.note: Engines that clamp the set to [DTSTART, ...).

rationale: Breaks the widely assumed invariant 'DTSTART is the minimum of the recurrence set'. Any product that uses DTSTART as a query lower bound is wrong under the 'include' reading.

title: EXDATE alone with no RRULE

cases.label: empty
cases.note: DTSTART is an instance and the EXDATE removes it: an event that exists and never occurs.

cases.label: dtstart-survives
cases.note: Engines where DTSTART is a seed outside the set and therefore not excludable.

rationale: The minimal probe of DTSTART's membership in the set; one line of input distinguishes the two models.

title: RDATE and RRULE producing instants one second apart

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.8.5.3 (Recurrence Rule)
normative.quote: Where duplicate instances are generated ... only one recurrence is considered.

expect.note: Four instances. Engines that de-duplicate at date granularity, or that compare with a tolerance, collapse these to three.

rationale: Pins the granularity of the de-duplication rule that SET-007 establishes.
